# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 82 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 82 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_082_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 8 — The Tower and the Seal

**1** "Is there no one else who can enter the tower?" I asked. "There are those who have already entered," he said, "and those who haven't yet — but will. **2** Anyone who refuses to repent will not enter the tower." **3** "So what do the repentant ones need to do to qualify for entry?" I asked. **4** "Their branches will be cut off and replanted by the one who distributed them originally. If any of them take root and don't wither, they will live. If any wither, they will die." **5** "But Lord," I said, "what if someone has repented but hasn't actually cleaned up their life or started living rightly? Will they still get into the tower?" "Repentance without fruit won't get them in," he said. "They have to produce fruit that proves their repentance is real." **6** "But shouldn't their branches be taken back since they returned them? And didn't they receive the seal?" **7** "No," he said. "The seal belongs to the water. People go down into the water spiritually dead and come up alive. That is why the seal was also announced to them — and through it they enter God's kingdom." **8** "But then why, Lord, did the forty stones come up from the deep first and get fitted into the foundational positions of the tower — the corners and sides?" **9** "Because they were the first believers," he said, "the foremost among the righteous — the apostles and teachers who proclaimed the name of the Son of God and died in the power and faith of the Son of God." **10** "And why did the virgins also help build the tower, carrying the stones?" **11** "Because they are holy spirits — the very powers of the Son of God. Without them, no one enters God's kingdom. If someone claims the name of God but doesn't receive the clothing these virgins provide, it does them no good at all. These virgins are the powers of the Son of God."

---

*PNEUMA makes the baptismal theology of v. 7 explicit — "dead and come up alive" — and renders the virgins' role in direct terms.*
